Identify the outliers of a JDemetra+ model

Source: R/outliers.R
outliers.jd3_model.Rd

Returns the outlying observations detected (or specified) in the pre-adjustment model of a model fitted with X13(), TRAMOSEATS(), REGARIMA() or TRAMO(): additive outliers (AO), level shifts (LS), transitory changes (TC) and seasonal outliers (SO). An outlier is dated at one observation, even when its effect (e.g. a level shift) lasts longer.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'jd3_model'
outliers(object, type = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted jd3_model (usually a column of a mable).

type

Optional character vector of outlier types to keep, e.g. c("AO", "LS"). NULL (default) keeps all of them.

...

Currently unused.

Value

For a jd3_model, an integer vector with the row positions of the outliers in the data of the model (the contract of fabletools::outliers()). Called on a mable, outliers() returns the corresponding rows of the data, with the key columns and .model. The type, estimate and test statistics of the outliers are available in tidy().

See also

X13(), TRAMOSEATS(), jd3_model_methods

Examples

mb <- model(tsibble::as_tsibble(AirPassengers), x13 = X13(value))

# Rows of the data that are outliers
outliers(mb)
#> # A tsibble: 1 x 3 [1M]
#> # Key:       .model [1]
#>   .model    index value
#>   <chr>     <mth> <dbl>
#> 1 x13    1951 May   172

# Additive outliers only
outliers(mb, type = "AO")
#> # A tsibble: 1 x 3 [1M]
#> # Key:       .model [1]
#>   .model    index value
#>   <chr>     <mth> <dbl>
#> 1 x13    1951 May   172
